root_idea.summary: Hardness or solidity, extended from a hard physical object to hardness of the heart.
root_idea.development: The lexical orientation moves from physical hardness or solidity to the condition of a heart becoming hard or remaining hard-hearted; مُقَاسَاة denotes dealing with or undergoing that condition.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Canonical Form I verb group, normalized to the Classical Arabic perfect citation form.
Canonical active-participle group, normalized from the inflected feminine Quranic form to the singular citation form.
Canonical abstract noun group with its own distinct lexical headword.

senses.definition: To become hard or hardened; of hearts, to become hard-hearted.
senses.usage_conditions: Quranic Form I perfect usage describing a change into hardness of heart.

senses.definition: Hard-hearted or hardened, characterized by hardness of heart.
senses.usage_conditions: Quranic active-participle usage describing hearts as hard or hardened.

senses.definition: Not pure or not genuine, in the reported variant reading قَسِيَّةً.
senses.usage_conditions: This variant interpretation is attached to the Quranic passage at 5:13 and is explained by comparison with قَسِيّ, a debased silver coin. It is not a separate canonical QAC form or occurrence.
Quranic abstract-noun usage describing the hardened condition of hearts.

other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical physical sense, illustrated by a hard stone; distinct from the Quranic description of hearts as hard-hearted.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The treatment, undergoing, or grappling with hardness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived noun denoting dealing with the condition of hardness rather than the condition itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A debased or adulterated silver coin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical coin term; it also supplies the comparison used for the reported Quranic interpretation “not pure.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: Solidity or hardness, including the hardness of debased silver.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical noun for physical hardness or solidity.

cautions: The interpretation “not pure” is associated with the reported variant reading قَسِيَّةً at 5:13, not with an additional canonical QAC occurrence.
No Lane or Maqayis entries were supplied; the root-level and Classical coverage here is therefore based on the supplied Quran-focused lexical discussion.
